reason: A permitted regional NOAA California Current LME aragonite indicator is available and reports a 2019–2024 downward trend, but the opened NOAA page provides no exact saturation value for a year and the underlying monthly gridded NetCDF values were not extracted. Keep a gap rather than score a trend as Ωar.
nearest_data: NOAA National Marine Ecosystem Status, California Current Aragonite: 2019–2024 sea-surface Ωar showed a downward trend and was mostly within its historical range (https://www.ecowatch.noaa.gov/regions/california-current; archived evidence/7d1e47fee8b272e4.png/.html/.txt, captured 2026-10-23T02:49:39.438Z). Its source-method text says regional averages are derived from mapped pCO2 and ESPER-estimated total alkalinity, with uncertainty propagated. NOAA/NCEI Accession 0287551 describes monthly 0.25° gridded model output for 1998–2025, revised 2026-09-15, with Ωar and uncertainty (https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/oceans/ncei/ocads/metadata/0287551.html). The 2024 peer-reviewed method paper describes 1998–2022 monthly grids and regional means but no single annual Ωar number was extracted. City/county measurements remain unavailable; the California Current is regional proxy/context only.
